mainTopic: Latecomers and קדושה (a דבר שבקדושה needs ten); no interrupting the עמידה; and whether רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי engage in holy words
overview: This amud begins mid-sentence, finishing a צריכא that explains why two rulings about praying a second time are both needed. Then רב הונא and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree about when a latecomer may start his own עמידה while the צבור is praying. For רב הונא the deadline is מודים, and for רבי יהושע בן לוי it is קדושה. The גמרא explains that the dispute depends on whether a יחיד may say קדושה. It brings the source that any דבר שבקדושה needs ten, learned through a גזירה שוה of 'תוך'. Everyone agrees that a person in the middle of his עמידה does not stop for קדושה, and the הלכה is that he does not stop even for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'. The גמרא then returns to the משנה, where רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say ברכות. It asks how this fits with the rule that a בעל קרי is forbidden in דברי תורה. Along the way it proves that רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses only in ספר דברים, and that he needs the חורב verses for a different teaching. Finally, a משנה about immersion seems to show that רבי יהודה does require טבילה for a plain בעל קרי. The גמרא rejects a suggested way around this, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First half of the explanation: why the synagogue ruling is needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the 'stop in the middle' ruling, we might think it applies only when both prayers are of the same type. One person praying both times alone, or both times with a צבור, would be covered. Joining a צבור after praying alone might be treated as though he never prayed. So the בית הכנסת ruling is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: …or a congregation and a congregation. But an individual compared to a congregation is considered like someone who has not prayed. That is why the second ruling teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began on the previous amud (21a). It explains why we need the ruling about someone who already prayed and then enters a בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'stop in the middle' ruling alone might only apply when the second prayer matches the first: יחיד with יחיד, or צבור with צבור. We could have thought that praying with a צבור after praying alone is a new, higher level, as if he never prayed. The בית הכנסת ruling teaches that this is not so: even then, he does not simply pray again.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual praying alone
A congregation (a מנין of ten)
Is considered like one who did not pray
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'או צבור וצבור' continue 'הני מילי יחיד ויחיד' from the end of the previous amud (21a).

phrases.english: but an individual in relation to a congregation

phrases.english: is like one who did not pray,

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל יחיד לגבי צבור כמאן דלא צלי דמי, קמשמע לן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first half of a צריכא begun earlier.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: showing that each ruling teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Praying with a צבור after praying alone might count as a fresh obligation, so he could pray again.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even יחיד followed by צבור is not treated as 'never prayed'. The בית הכנסת ruling teaches this.

steps.title: Second half of the explanation: why the 'stop in the middle' ruling is needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the בית הכנסת ruling, we might think its reason is that he had not started yet. Someone already in the middle might be allowed to continue. So the 'stop in the middle' ruling is also needed. Both rulings are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us only here (the synagogue case), I would say the reason is that he had not yet begun. But there, where he already began, say he does not stop. Therefore both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side: why we also need the ruling about someone who is already in the middle of praying. It then concludes that both rulings are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית הכנסת case is about someone who has not started a second prayer yet. Holding back from starting is easier than stopping a prayer midway. So we might think a person already in the middle may finish. The 'stop in the middle' ruling teaches that he must stop, even in the middle of a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it had taught us (only) here
He began it (the prayer)
I would say no (the rule does not apply)
It is necessary, meaning both teachings are needed

steps.whatToRemember: Both rulings are needed. One teaches that praying with a צבור after praying alone is no excuse to pray again. The other teaches that even someone already in the middle must stop.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only here,
phrases.notes: Here = one who already prayed and enters a synagogue.

phrases.english: (I would say it is) because he had not begun it,
but there, where he did begin it —
phrases.notes: There = he is standing in prayer and remembers he already prayed.

phrases.english: say that he need not stop.
Therefore both are necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואי אשמעינן הכא, משום דלא אתחיל בה

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once he has started praying again, he may finish.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must stop even midway, so both rulings are needed.

steps.title: רב הונא: a latecomer may start only if he can finish before מודים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules about someone who has not yet prayed and finds the צבור in the middle of the עמידה. He should pray only if he can finish before the שליח צבור reaches מודים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: One who enters a בית הכנסת and finds the צבור praying should pray if he can begin and finish before the שליח צבור reaches 'מודים'. If not, he should not pray (now).
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא gives a time limit for a latecomer who wants to say his own עמידה while the צבור is praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that he should not be in the middle of his own private prayer when the צבור says מודים. At that point everyone bows together, and he would look like he is not joining in. If he cannot finish in time, he should wait and pray afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader (chazzan)
The ברכה of thanksgiving in the עמידה, where everyone bows
To begin and to finish
Synagogue

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One who enters a synagogue
phrases.notes: He has not yet prayed.

phrases.english: and found the congregation praying,
phrases.notes: They are saying the עמידה.

phrases.english: if he can begin and finish

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעַ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר לְ״מוֹדִים״ — יִתְפַּלֵּל.
phrases.english: before the prayer leader reaches 'Modim', he should pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא: הנכנס לבית הכנסת ומצא צבור שמתפללין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related topic about a latecomer who has not yet prayed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may start his own עמידה only if he can finish before the שליח צבור reaches מודים.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the deadline is קדושה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי sets an earlier deadline. The latecomer may start only if he can finish before the שליח צבור reaches קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If he can begin and finish before the שליח צבור reaches 'קדושה', he should pray. If not, he should not pray.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different time limit for the same case. This sets up a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדושה comes before מודים in the חזרת הש״ץ, so this is a stricter, earlier deadline. רבי יהושע בן לוי wants the latecomer free to answer קדושה with the צבור. The גמרא will explain why the two אמוראים differ.

keyTerms.meaning: The communal sanctification ('נקדש / קדוש קדוש קדוש') said in the חזרת הש״ץ

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If he can begin and finish

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעַ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר לִ״קְדוּשָּׁה״ — יִתְפַּלֵּל,
phrases.english: before the prayer leader reaches 'Kedushah', he should pray,
and if not, he should not pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע בן לוי אמר: אם יכול להתחיל ולגמור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing ruling on the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may start only if he can finish before the שליח צבור reaches קדושה.

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle underlies the dispute between רב הונא and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that the latecomer must finish his prayer by some point in the חזרת הש״ץ. The question is why one picks מודים and the other picks קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רב הונא from רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: The dispute: may an individual say קדושה?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that a יחיד may say קדושה alone, so he does not need to finish before the צבור's קדושה. רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that a יחיד may not say קדושה, so he must finish in time to say it with the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that an individual may say קדושה, and the other master holds that an individual may not say קדושה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two opinions depend on whether a person praying alone may say קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a יחיד may say קדושה on his own, missing the צבור's קדושה is no loss. Then the only deadline is מודים, where he must bow together with everyone. If a יחיד may not say קדושה, this is his only chance to say it. So he must be finished in time to answer with the צבור.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds
An individual does not say

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' is רב הונא (the יחיד may say קדושה). The second 'מר' is רבי יהושע בן לוי (the יחיד may not).

phrases.english: One master holds an individual may say 'Kedushah',
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא.

phrases.english: and the other master holds an individual may not say 'Kedushah'.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute depends on whether a יחיד may say קדושה. רב הונא says yes; רבי יהושע בן לוי says no.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: a פסוק shows קדושה needs ten
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה supports the view that a יחיד may not say קדושה. He learns it from the פסוק 'ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל', which teaches that any דבר שבקדושה needs at least ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, רב אדא בר אהבה said: From where do we know that an individual may not say קדושה? As it says, 'And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel.' Any matter of holiness may not be done with fewer than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement that agrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי. It gives a פסוק as the source for the rule that a יחיד may not say קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בתוך' (among) shows that sanctifying הקב״ה must happen within a community, meaning ten. So קדושה, which is a דבר שבקדושה, cannot be said by someone praying alone. This gives a scriptural basis to רבי יהושע בן לוי's position.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said (introduces a supporting statement)
From where (is it derived)?
'And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel' (ויקרא כב:לב)
A matter of holiness (קדושה, קדיש, ברכו, and the like)
Ten, i.e., a מנין

steps.whatToRemember: Any דבר שבקדושה requires a מנין of ten, based on 'ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל'. This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who holds that a latecomer should finish before קדושה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the halacha that קדושה, קדיש, ברכו and similar parts of prayer require a מנין.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: And similarly Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
From where do we know that an individual does not say 'Kedushah'?
As it says: 'And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel',
phrases.notes: ויקרא כב:לב

phrases.english: any matter of holiness
may not be with fewer than ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וכן אמר רב אדא בר אהבה: מנין שאין היחיד אומר קדושה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the second opinion in the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבי יהושע בן לוי that a יחיד may not say קדושה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כב:לב, 'ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל', as derived by רב אדא בר אהבה.

steps.title: How does the verse teach the need for ten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק 'ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל' shows that ten people are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that 'בתוך בני ישראל' means a group of ten. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רב אדא בר אהבה said this פסוק teaches that a דבר שבקדושה needs ten. But the פסוק never says the number ten. So the גמרא asks where the number comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it implied? Where do we see it in the words?

phrases.english: How is it implied?
phrases.notes: It refers to the derivation from 'ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל' in step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the mechanism behind the derivation in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word 'בתוך' in the פסוק points to the number ten.

steps.title: Linking 'among' to 'among' to get ten
steps.stepSummary: רבנאי teaches a גזירה שוה. The word 'תוך' appears in our פסוק and also in the story of קרח's group. That group was ten, so here too we need ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבנאי, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא, taught: we learn it from 'among' and 'among.' Here it is written, 'And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel.' There it is written, 'Separate yourselves from among this congregation.' Just as there it means ten, so too here it means ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The same word 'תוך' appears in two פסוקים, so we can learn one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story of קרח, 'מתוך העדה' refers to an 'עדה', a congregation. An עדה is ten, learned from the ten מרגלים, who are called 'העדה הרעה'. Since our פסוק shares the word 'תוך' with that one, the meaning 'ten' carries over. This is why קדושה needs ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one פסוק from another because they share the same word
It comes (is learned) from
Among / in the midst of
Congregation; an עדה is ten people
Just as there, so too here

steps.confusionAlert: The number ten is not written in the קרח פסוק either. It comes from a second link: the word 'עדה' is also used for the ten מרגלים. There are two steps: תוך→תוך, then עדה→עדה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that קדושה, קדיש, ברכו and other דברים שבקדושה need a מנין of ten.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי רַבְנַאי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: As Rabbenai, the brother of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, taught:
It is learned from 'among' and 'among.'
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה built on a shared word.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel,'
and it is written there: 'Separate yourselves from among this congregation,'
phrases.notes: This is the story of קרח (במדבר טז:כא).

phrases.english: Just as there it means ten,
so too here it means ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַבְנַאי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by explaining how the number is derived.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'תוך' links our פסוק to 'מתוך העדה'. An עדה is ten, so קדושה needs ten.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no stopping for קדושה
steps.stepSummary: Both רב הונא and רבי יהושע בן לוי agree that someone in the middle of his own תפלה does not stop to say קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in any case, everyone agrees that one does not interrupt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a point that both sides of the argument share. A person already in the middle of his עמידה does not stop to answer קדושה with the צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two views argued only about when a latecomer may start. Once he is already praying, both agree he keeps going and does not interrupt for קדושה. That is exactly why רבי יהושע בן לוי wanted him to finish before the צבור reaches קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
In any case / at least
He certainly does not interrupt

phrases.english: And according to everyone, in any case,
he does not interrupt (his prayer for קדושה).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת מִפְסָק לָא פָּסֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dispute in steps 3-7 by stating the point of agreement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A person in the middle of תפלה does not interrupt to say קדושה. This holds according to all views.

steps.title: May one stop for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'?
steps.stepSummary: The ישיבה asks whether a person in the middle of תפלה may stop to answer 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך' in קדיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: may one interrupt to say 'May His great name be blessed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question. We know he does not stop for קדושה, but what about the main answer of קדיש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question builds on step 10. Perhaps 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך' is so important that it is an exception, even though קדושה is not.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (the scholars)
To interrupt
'May His great name be blessed', the central response of קדיש

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about interrupting
to say 'May His great name be blessed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 10 to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך' is important enough to justify interrupting תפלה.

steps.title: רב דימי's report: stop only for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of תלמידי רבי יוחנן that one interrupts for nothing except 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'. Even someone learning מעשה מרכבה stops for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, students of רבי יוחנן, say: we do not interrupt for anything except 'May His great name be blessed.' Even someone busy with the study of the Divine Chariot stops for it.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is brought from ארץ ישראל. It treats 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך' as a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשה מרכבה is the highest and holiest kind of learning. If even that is interrupted for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך', it shows how important this response is. So by this view, תפלה would also be interrupted for it.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Students of
Except for
The mystical study of the Divine Chariot (יחזקאל א)
He stops

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,
students of Rabbi Yoḥanan, say:
For everything, we do not interrupt,
except for 'May His great name be blessed.'
For even one busy with the study of the Divine Chariot
stops (to say it).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a reported tradition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By this view, one interrupts even תפלה for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך', but for nothing else.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow this view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like the view reported by רב דימי. One does not interrupt תפלה even for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. It rejects the view that one stops the עמידה for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report in step 12 is a real opinion, but it is not accepted as practical הלכה. So the rule from step 10 stays in place for קדיש too: in the middle of תפלה, you do not interrupt.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: In the middle of the עמידה, one does not stop for קדושה or for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'. Ten are needed for any דבר שבקדושה, learned from the גזירה שוה of 'תוך'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical halachic outcome: a person in the middle of the עמידה stays silent and does not answer קדיש or קדושה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is not in accordance with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the view reported in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One does not interrupt תפלה even for 'יהא שמו הגדול מברך'.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say the ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. There רבי יהודה says a בעל קרי says the ברכות before and after קריאת שמע, and before and after food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he recites the blessings before them and after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes רבי יהודה's view about a בעל קרי so it can analyze that view next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא in the משנה said a בעל קרי only thinks שמע in his heart and says no ברכות before or after it. For food he says only the ברכה after the meal. רבי יהודה disagrees and says he says the ברכות both before and after, in both cases. This seems to suggest that רבי יהודה allows a בעל קרי to engage in holy words.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission and has not yet immersed
He says the blessings before them and after them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He recites a blessing before them and after them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means קריאת שמע and food, from the משנה on 20b.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מְבָרֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם וּלְאַחֲרֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to the משנה's discussion of a בעל קרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a בעל קרי says the ברכות before and after שמע and food.

steps.title: But a בעל קרי is forbidden in דברי תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה really allows a בעל קרי to learn תורה. It challenges this from רבי יהושע בן לוי, who derives from מתן תורה that a בעל קרי is forbidden in דברי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי יהודה holds a בעל קרי is permitted in words of תורה? But רבי יהושע בן לוי said: where do we learn that a בעל קרי is forbidden in words of תורה? It says, 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,' and next to it, 'The day that you stood (before ה׳ at חורב).' Just as there בעלי קרי were forbidden, so too here בעלי קרי are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading of רבי יהודה's view. If he lets a בעל קרי say ברכות, does he also allow him to learn תורה? That seems to contradict a teaching from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי uses a סמיכות. The פסוק about teaching תורה to your children is placed right next to the פסוק about standing at הר סיני. At סיני, בעלי קרי had to separate and immerse, so in all learning of תורה a בעל קרי is forbidden. This seems to clash with רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...?
But didn't (so-and-so) say...!
Words of תורה; תורה learning
Juxtaposed / placed next to it

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not just about ברכות. The גמרא infers that if רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say ברכות, he must also allow תורה learning. That inference is what clashes with רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Yehuda holds
that a man who had a seminal emission is permitted in words of Torah?
But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
From where do we know regarding one who had a seminal emission
that he is forbidden in words of Torah?
As it says: 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,'
phrases.notes: דברים ד:ט, which refers to teaching תורה.

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'The day that you stood, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים ד:י, which refers to standing at הר סיני.

phrases.english: Just as there, those who had seminal emissions were forbidden,
so too here, those who had seminal emissions are forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְקָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּעַל קֶרִי מוּתָּר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of רבי יהודה's view quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that רבי יהודה permits a בעל קרי to engage in דברי תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי learns from the סמיכות of the פסוקים that a בעל קרי is forbidden in תורה, just as at סיני. So how can רבי יהודה allow him to say ברכות?

steps.title: Blocking the defense that רבי יהודה never learns from neighboring verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא imagines a defense for רבי יהודה: he does not learn from neighboring verses at all. It rejects this using רב יוסף's rule that רבי יהודה does learn from them in משנה תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that רבי יהודה does not learn from neighboring verses, didn't רב יוסף say: even someone who does not learn from neighboring verses in the whole תורה does learn from them in משנה תורה? For רבי יהודה does not learn from neighboring verses in the whole תורה, but in משנה תורה he does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out for רבי יהודה and immediately shuts it down. The question from Step 15 still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule against a בעל קרי learning comes from two verses side by side in ספר דברים. So someone could say רבי יהודה simply rejects that kind of reading. רב יוסף answers that רבי יהודה rejects סמוכים everywhere except in ספר דברים, and this proof comes from exactly there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say': introduces a possible answer that the גמרא is about to reject
Expounds; learns a law out of a verse
Verses placed next to each other, read as teaching a shared law
ספר דברים, the fifth book of the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not someone who accepts סמוכים everywhere or rejects them everywhere. His position is split: no in most of the תורה, yes in ספר דברים. That split is why the question from Step 15 still works.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this passage sets out to prove both halves of רב יוסף's statement.

phrases.english: And if you will say that Rabbi Yehuda
does not expound juxtaposed verses,
but didn't Rav Yosef say:
Even one who does not expound juxtaposed verses
throughout the Torah does expound them in Deuteronomy.
For Rabbi Yehuda does not expound juxtaposed verses
throughout the entire Torah,
yet in Deuteronomy he does expound them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ סְמוּכִים, וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible defense against the challenge in Step 15, so the challenge keeps its force.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יהודה never learns from neighboring verses.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה does learn from neighboring verses in ספר דברים, which is where רבי יהושע בן לוי's source comes from.

steps.title: Where do we see that רבי יהודה rejects neighboring verses in the rest of the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the first half of רב יוסף's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the whole תורה, how do we know that he does not learn from neighboring verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants proof for the first half of רב יוסף's statement. This line sets up a ברייתא that will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף made a two-part claim. The גמרא will now prove each part separately, starting with the claim that רבי יהודה rejects סמוכים outside ספר דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
All of it; the entire

phrases.english: And throughout the entire Torah,
from where do we know that he does not expound?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ מְנָא לַן דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the first half of רב יוסף's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that רבי יהודה rejects סמוכים in the rest of the תורה.

steps.title: בן עזאי learns a מכשפה's death penalty from the neighboring verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings בן עזאי. He learns that a מכשפה is killed by סקילה because her verse sits next to the verse about one who lies with an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: בן עזאי says, it says 'A sorceress you shall not let live,' and it says 'Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.' The תורה placed them side by side to teach: just as one who lies with an animal is stoned, so too a sorceress is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where בן עזאי uses neighboring verses to find a death penalty. This sets up רבי יהודה's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about a מכשפה does not say how she is executed. The very next verse, about lying with an animal, belongs to a sin we know is punished by סקילה. בן עזאי reasons that the two verses share that punishment because they sit side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
A sorceress
The תורה placed this topic right next to that one
Stoning, a court death penalty

phrases.english: As it was taught: Ben Azzai says:
It is stated: "You shall not allow a sorceress to live,"
and it is stated: "Whoever lies with a beast
shall surely be put to death."
It juxtaposed this matter to that, to say:
just as one who lies with a beast is stoned,
so too a sorceress is stoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the ברייתא that answers the question in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מכשפה is killed by סקילה, learned from the neighboring verse about one who lies with an animal.

steps.title: רבי יהודה rejects learning from neighboring verses and uses a different source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה refuses to sentence someone to stoning just because two verses are neighbors. He learns the same law from אוב and ידעוני instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: just because the תורה placed the verses side by side, should we take this person out to be stoned? Rather, אוב and ידעוני were already included among all the sorcerers. Why were they singled out? To compare to them and teach you: just as אוב and ידעוני are stoned, so too a sorceress is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה pushes back on בן עזאי's method. That pushback is the proof the גמרא wanted: outside ספר דברים, רבי יהודה does not learn from neighboring verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees with the result, that a מכשפה is stoned. He rejects the method of סמוכים. He uses a different rule instead: when the תורה pulls a specific case (אוב and ידעוני) out of a general group (sorcerers), it teaches something about the whole group.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we take him out to be stoned?
Two types of sorcery: a medium and a wizard
To compare one case to another
Rather; introduces a replacement explanation

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה and בן עזאי do not disagree about the law. Both say a מכשפה is stoned. They only disagree about how we know it. The גמרא cares about the method, not the result.
steps.whatToRemember: Outside ספר דברים, רבי יהודה does not learn from neighboring verses. He finds a different source even when he agrees with the result.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
And just because it juxtaposed this matter to that,
shall we take this one out to be stoned?
Rather: the medium and the wizard
were included among all the sorcerers,
and why were they singled out?
To compare to them and to tell you:
just as a medium and a wizard are stoned,
so too a sorceress is stoned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסְּמָכוֹ עִנְיָן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה rejects בן עזאי's method. This proves the first half of רב יוסף's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using neighboring verses to decide a death penalty, outside ספר דברים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Placing two verses side by side is too weak a basis for sentencing someone to stoning. A stronger source is needed.

steps.title: Where do we see that רבי יהודה does learn from neighboring verses in ספר דברים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the second half of רב יוסף's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in משנה תורה, how do we know that he does learn from neighboring verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now wants proof for the second half of רב יוסף's statement. This line sets up the next ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half is now proven. This second half is the part that keeps the question against רבי יהודה alive.

keyTerms.meaning: That he does expound

phrases.english: And in Deuteronomy,
from where do we know that he does expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from proving the first half of רב יוסף's rule to the second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses in ספר דברים.

steps.title: A ברייתא about marrying a woman violated by one's father or son
steps.stepSummary: The proof begins with רבי אליעזר. He allows a man to marry a woman his father or son forced or seduced. רבי יהודה's opposing view, which supplies the actual proof, comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, a man may marry a woman forced by his father, or seduced by his father, or forced by his son, or seduced by his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא that will prove its point. This first line is setup: רבי אליעזר's permissive view comes first, and רבי יהודה's response follows next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids a man to marry his father's wife or his son's wife. רבי אליעזר holds that a woman who was only forced or seduced, never married to them, is not included. The proof will come when רבי יהודה forbids the forced woman of one's father, based on two neighboring verses in ספר דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was forced (raped)
A woman who was seduced
Marries

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A man may marry a woman raped by his father
and one seduced by his father,
one raped by his son and one seduced by his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר נוֹשֵׂא אָדָם אֲנוּסַת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that answers the question in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses in ספר דברים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי אליעזר's permissive view. רבי יהודה's opposing view, based on neighboring verses, follows next.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids marrying a woman his father raped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids a man to marry a woman his father raped or seduced. רב גידל in the name of רב explains why: the verse says not to uncover 'his father's skirt.' That means any woman his father has been with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה forbids a man to marry a woman his father raped or seduced. רב גידל said in the name of רב: What is רבי יהודה's reason? The verse says, 'A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's skirt.' A 'skirt' his father has seen, he may not uncover.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the proof begun in step 21. רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי אליעזר and forbids the marriage, and רב explains which verse he uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'his father's wife' cover a woman the father married. The extra words 'his father's skirt' widen the ban to any woman the father was with, even without marriage. So far this is only the verse. The link to neighboring verses comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman his father raped
a woman his father seduced
'his father's skirt,' meaning a woman his father was intimate with
what is the reason?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits
a woman raped by his father and a woman seduced by his father.
And Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
What is Rabbi Yehuda's reason?

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו
phrases.english: As it is written: "A man shall not take his father's wife,
and shall not uncover his father's skirt."
A skirt that his father has seen, he may not uncover.
phrases.notes: Any woman the father was with is forbidden to the son.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר בַּאֲנוּסַת אָבִיו וּבִמְפוּתַּת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies רבי יהודה's opposing view, which the proof begun in step 21 depends on.
steps.raayaObject: The second half of רב יוסף's rule: in משנה תורה, רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling forbidding אנוסת אביו, as explained by רב גידל in the name of רב.

steps.title: The verse is about a raped woman because it sits next to the rape passage
steps.stepSummary: How do we know the verse 'his father's skirt' is about a woman the father raped? Because the verse right before it deals with rape. This shows that רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this verse is talking about a woman his father raped? Because right next to it is the verse 'And the man who lay with her shall give...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know the 'skirt' verse is about rape and answers right away: it sits next to the rape passage. This completes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the verse itself mentions rape. The rape case comes only from the neighboring passage (דברים כב:כט). Since רבי יהודה relies on that, we see that in משנה תורה he does use סמוכין, just as רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where do we know?
because it is placed right next to it
and so on (the verse continues)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה does not learn from neighboring verses in most of the תורה, but he does in ספר דברים (משנה תורה). His ban on אנוסת אביו proves it.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is written about a woman raped by his father?
Because placed next to it is:
"And the man who lay with her shall give..." etc.
phrases.notes: This is the passage about the fine paid by a rapist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the hidden step in רבי יהודה's reading: a neighboring verse.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה uses סמוכין in משנה תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'skirt' verse (דברים כג:א) sits next to the rape passage (דברים כב:כט).

steps.title: רבי יהודה needs the חורב verses for a different teaching
steps.stepSummary: Behind this step is a question the גמרא does not say out loud. If רבי יהודה learns from neighbors in דברים, why doesn't he forbid a בעל קרי to learn תורה, based on the neighboring verses about חורב? The answer: he does learn from neighbors in דברים, but he needs these particular verses for another teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: Yes, in משנה תורה he learns from neighboring verses. But he needs these neighboring verses for the other teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unstated challenge. If רבי יהודה uses neighbors in דברים, he should forbid a בעל קרי to study תורה from 'והודעתם לבניך' next to 'בחורב'. The answer is that those verses are already used for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, the ban on a בעל קרי learning תורה was learned from these neighboring verses: just as at חורב people kept away from קרי, so too when teaching תורה. רבי יהודה does not hold that ban. The answer is not that he rejects neighbors in דברים. Rather, these verses are 'taken' by a different lesson, so they cannot also teach the בעל קרי rule.

keyTerms.meaning: they said (introduces an answer)
yes, indeed
ספר דברים
he needs it for (a different purpose)
juxtaposed (neighboring) verses

steps.confusionAlert: The question being answered is never written in the text. It is implied: 'Then why doesn't רבי יהודה forbid a בעל קרי to learn תורה?' Without knowing that, the answer 'אמרי' seems to come from nowhere.

phrases.english: They said:
Indeed, in Mishneh Torah he does expound juxtapositions,
but these juxtaposed verses he needs
for the other teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהודה against a problem raised by the proof in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that a בעל קרי may learn Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he uses neighboring verses in דברים, the חורב verses should force him to forbid a בעל קרי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verses are needed for another teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using סמוכין in דברים should commit רבי יהודה to the בעל קרי ban.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חורב verses are used for רבי יהושע בן לוי's other teaching, so they cannot teach the בעל קרי ban.

steps.title: Teaching your son תורה is like receiving it at סיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches: whoever teaches his son תורה is considered as if he received it at הר חורב. He learns this because 'make them known to your children' sits right next to 'the day you stood before ה׳ at חורב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Whoever teaches his son תורה, the verse treats him as if he received it from הר חורב. As it says, 'Make them known to your children and your children's children,' and right after it is written, 'The day you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the 'other teaching' of רבי יהושע בן לוי that רבי יהודה uses these neighboring verses for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching uses the same neighboring pair of verses: teaching children, then standing at חורב. Since the pair already teaches the greatness of teaching your son, רבי יהודה does not take a second lesson (the בעל קרי ban) from it.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse treats him as if
Mount Horeb, הר סיני
and you shall make them known to your children
after it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is also a well-known teaching about the value of teaching Torah to one's children.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Whoever teaches his son Torah,
the verse credits him
as if he received it from Mount Horeb.
As it says: "And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,"
and it is written after it:

phrases.aramaic: ״יוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַדְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּחוֹרֵב״.
phrases.english: "The day that you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching mentioned in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching one's son Torah is like receiving it at חורב, learned from neighboring verses in דברים ד.

steps.title: A משנה where רבי יהודה exempts people from immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. A זב who had a seminal emission, a נדה who discharged semen, and a woman who saw blood during relations all need טבילה. רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: A זב who had a seminal emission, a נדה who discharged semen, and a woman who saw blood during relations all need immersion. רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבי יהודה's ruling in our משנה. It quotes a משנה about immersion for קרי, and the next step draws an inference from it about רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these people already have a stronger, longer impurity. Still, the חכמים say they must immerse for the קרי so they can learn תורה. רבי יהודה exempts them. The גמרא will infer that he exempts only these special cases, so a plain בעל קרי would need immersion before learning תורה. That would contradict his ruling that a בעל קרי may say ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned in a משנה
a man with an impure discharge
a seminal emission
immersion in a מקוה
exempts

phrases.english: We learned in a mishna: a zav who experienced a seminal emission,
and a menstruating woman who discharged semen,
and a woman who had relations and saw blood,
require immersion.
And Rabbi Yehuda exempts them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the סמוכין answer in steps 24-25, the גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבי יהודה's ruling from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים require immersion for קרי even for people already under a stronger impurity, and רבי יהודה exempts them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה only exempted the זב, not a plain בעל קרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's exemption in the משנה is limited to a זב who had an emission, because that person could not become pure through טבילה anyway. A plain בעל קרי still needs טבילה even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה only exempted a זב who had a seminal emission, because from the start he was not someone who could be purified by immersion. But a person who only had a seminal emission is required to immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its challenge from the משנה. רבי יהודה's exemption applies only to a זב, so for an ordinary בעל קרי he requires טבילה. That seems to contradict his ruling that a בעל קרי says ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב stays impure for seven days, so immersing for the קרי would not make him pure right now. That is why רבי יהודה says the immersion is pointless for him. A plain בעל קרי becomes pure the moment he immerses, so for him רבי יהודה agrees that טבילה is required.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Only up to here' — the opinion goes only this far and no further
A man with an abnormal discharge; he carries a seven-day impurity
Someone for whom immersion actually works to purify him
Alone, by itself, with no other impurity mixed in
Requires (immersion)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה holds that a בעל קרי never needs טבילה. His exemption depends on the special situation of the זב, whose immersion cannot work right now.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לֹא פָּטַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only exempted
phrases.notes: Limits how far רבי יהודה's ruling reaches

phrases.english: in the case of a zav who saw a seminal emission,
since from the outset he was not fit to be purified by immersion,
phrases.notes: He stays impure as a זב for seven days, so immersing now does not help

phrases.english: but one who had only a seminal emission, he requires (immersion).

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לֹא פָּטַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה in step 26: רבי יהודה exempts only a זב, so a plain בעל קרי needs טבילה. This clashes with his ruling in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in our משנה that a בעל קרי says ברכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה requires טבילה for a plain בעל קרי (exempting only a זב), he evidently treats a בעל קרי as restricted from holy words. So how can he let him say ברכות?

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה exempts even a plain בעל קרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a defense for רבי יהודה. Perhaps he exempts even a plain בעל קרי, and the משנה picked the זב case only to show how strict the רבנן are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: the same rule applies, and רבי יהודה exempts even a plain בעל קרי. They argue specifically about a זב who had an emission only to show you how far the רבנן's view reaches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out of the challenge in step 27. The זב case may not prove that רבי יהודה's exemption is limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the משנה chose the hardest case for the רבנן. Even when immersion seems useless, the רבנן still require it. If so, the choice of case shows the strength of the רבנן's position. It would tell us nothing about the limits of רבי יהודה's position.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say' — introduces a possible objection
The same law applies
To show you the strength (how far the opinion goes)

phrases.english: And if you say:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל קֶרִי גְּרֵידָא
phrases.english: the same is true that even one who had only a seminal emission
Rabbi Yehuda also exempts,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי דְּקָא מִפַּלְּגִי בְּזָב שֶׁרָאָה קֶרִי —
phrases.english: and the fact that they disagree about a zav who saw an emission —
is to show you the strength of the Rabbis' view.
phrases.notes: Even in the case where immersion seems useless, the רבנן still require it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a defense of רבי יהודה against the inference drawn in step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting why the משנה chose its case (להודיעך כחן דרבנן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה names the זב case, רבי יהודה must exempt only a זב and obligate a plain בעל קרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps he exempts every בעל קרי, and the זב case was chosen only to show the strength of the רבנן. Steps 29-31 reject this.

steps.title: Look at the last case of the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: To reject the objection, the גמרא points to the end of the משנה: a woman who saw blood during relations needs טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last part of the משנה: a woman who was having relations and saw blood needs immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא brings the last case of the משנה, which it will use in the next steps to knock down the objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been proven yet. The גמרא is putting a new piece of evidence on the table. The next steps will ask whose opinion this case follows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say the end' — look at the last part of the משנה
A woman engaged in marital relations
And she saw (menstrual) blood

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
a woman who was having relations and saw blood — requires immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the rejection of the defense suggested in step 28 by bringing the end of the משנה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested defense (step 28) that רבי יהודה exempts even a plain בעל קרי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The objection ignores the last case of the same משנה. The next steps will show that case only makes sense as רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: Whose view is the last case? Not the רבנן, because for them it is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the woman's case follows. It cannot be the רבנן, because if they require טבילה for a זב, they surely require it for a woman whose immersion would have worked at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? If you say the רבנן — that is obvious! The רבנן require immersion for a זב who had an emission, even though he could not be purified by immersion from the start. Then surely they require it for a woman who had relations and saw blood, who could be purified by immersion from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the author of the woman's case is. It shows that for the רבנן the case would add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the woman had relations, she was still pure, so an immersion for the semen would have worked. The blood came only afterward. The זב, by contrast, was already impure for seven days. So her case is easier than his, and anyone who requires immersion for him would surely require it for her. A משנה does not usually teach something that obvious, so this case cannot be the view of the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom is this taught?
'If you say' — introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to reject
Obvious — so why would the משנה need to say it?
Is it not all the more so? (a קל וחומר)
A woman for whom immersion works to purify her

phrases.english: According to whom is it taught?
If you say according to the Rabbis — that is obvious!
Now, if a zav who saw an emission —

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא לָאו בַּר טְבִילָה הוּא, מְחַיְּיבִי רַבָּנַן;
phrases.english: who from the outset was not fit for immersion — the Rabbis require (immersion);
a woman who had relations and saw blood —
who from the outset was fit for immersion,
phrases.notes: At the time of relations she was still pure, so immersing for the semen would have worked

phrases.english: is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the case brought in step 29 to find who its author is
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion the last case of the משנה follows

steps.title: So the last case is רבי יהודה's, taught for a precise reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the woman's case must follow רבי יהודה, and that the משנה taught it on purpose. This passage ends here, mid-sentence, and the next passage explains the point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not רבי יהודה's view, and the case was taught specifically…
steps.whatsHappening: Since the case cannot be the רבנן's view, the גמרא assigns it to רבי יהודה. It says the משנה stated it deliberately. This line leads straight into the next passage, where the גמרא will spell out what the case teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה requires טבילה for this woman, then he is not exempting every בעל קרי. 'דווקא' means the case was chosen with care. The next amud will show the contrast: only someone whose immersion would have worked needs it, while the זב does not. This rejects the defense in step 28 and restores the inference of step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, is it not…' — introduces the conclusion the גמרא is driving toward
Specifically, precisely — taught for an exact reason

steps.whyThisMatters: This defeats the suggested defense in step 28. רבי יהודה's exemption depends on whether the immersion could work, so he does require טבילה for a plain בעל קרי. That keeps the difficulty alive against his lenient ruling that a בעל קרי says ברכות, and the גמרא takes it up on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda's view,
and it was taught specifically,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 30: the case must be רבי יהודה's view
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not exempt every בעל קרי from טבילה (upholding the challenge of step 27 against the defense in step 28)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last case of the משנה: a woman who saw blood during relations needs טבילה
